newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, De Beers in consensus - ARS official.
newsitem.headline: Russia, De Beers in consensus - ARS official.

text.p: Russia and De Beers have reached a breakthrough on a delayed gem export agreement still awaiting presidential approval, and Moscow has dropped its previous objections to the deal, a gem official said on Monday.

"Consensus has been reached -- all of the government's questions have been dropped," said Valentin Logunov, spokesman for the Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS) diamond-producing monopoly, which is De Beers' negotiating partner.
"There were some concessions, that much is obvious -- but who gave up what, I don't know. Ask De Beers."
The South African gem group's Moscow representation was not immediately available for comment.
Logunov declined to say to what extent the final trade arrangement would deviate from a 1996 memorandum that was to form the basis of a formal agreement.
"The memorandum is a broad structure, and an agreement is a commercial arrangement," he said, adding, "the commercial arrangement has been drawn up."
He said that all that was needed now was President Boris Yeltsin's approval and government documents enforcing the deal.
First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin, quoted by Russian news agencies last week, said a formal deal could be signed this month or next.

Logunov said one talking point concerned the amount of gems ARS would sell outside De Beers on world markets, and that the memorandum had mentioned a quota of five percent of ARS' total output but that "there was a question of ten percent".
"This issue concerns how we will independently study the world diamond market, and not just rely on the highly-respected De Beers," he said.

De Beers stopped purchases of Russian diamonds at the end of last year when it cancelled its interim arrangement after Russia failed to approve or reject a new trade deal. Russia had said it had objections to the memorandum and called for changes.
